title: Casts from and to strings: trimmed, lenient parsing; Java's double text
verdict: parse: trims, `1.5` → `INT` raises (ANSI) or truncates; doubles accept `inf`, `nan`, `1.5d`, hex; text: `1.0E20`
description: Parsing trims whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) and takes a sign. To integers: `'1e3'`, `'0x10'`, `'12abc'`, `''`, `'1_000'` fail; `'1.5'` fails under ANSI and truncates to 1 without it. To doubles: `'nan'`, `'inf'`, `'Infinity'`, `'-infinity'`, `'+Inf'` (any case), `'1.5d'`, `'1.5f'`, `'0x1p3'` (Java's hex floats), `'.5'`, `'5.'` parse, `'-nan'` fails; `'1e400'` is +inf and `'1e-400'` 0, `'-10e-400'` -0.0 (a negative below the smallest double keeps its sign). To decimals the value rounds half up (`'1.005'` → 1.01) and an exponent is allowed. To booleans: `t`, `true`, `y`, `yes`, `1` and their opposites, any case. To dates: `2024`, `2024-01`, `2024-1-5` and a trailing time parse; `2024-02-30` fails; `+10000-01-01` parses.
A failure raises `CAST_INVALID_INPUT` under ANSI and is NULL without it; `try_cast` gives NULL in both.

Formatting: doubles print as Java's `Double.toString` (`1.0E20`, `1.0E-5`, `0.001`, `1.0E7`, `1.23456789E8`, `-0.0`, `NaN`, `Infinity`); floats as `Float.toString` (`0.1`). Decimals keep their scale (`1.50`); under ANSI they print plainly (`0.0000001000`), without it in scientific notation (`1.000E-7`). Dates print with a sign past 9999, timestamps without trailing zeros (`10:00:00.12`), arrays as `[1, null]`, structs as `{1, null}`.
reference: Casts to and from strings follow the reference's `cast` rules; `cast_failure` as the cast states. Spark's parsing is more lenient (trimming, hex floats, `1.5d`) and its double text is Java's, so a writer checks the text before the cast and formats doubles itself.

evidence.note: string casts: `UTF8StringUtils.toLongExact` under ANSI, `toLong` returning NULL otherwise

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: The same with ANSI off is 1: truncated
The same with ANSI off is NULL
`cast(' 1\t' as tinyint)` is 1: spaces and tabs trimmed
An array with a NULL cast to string prints as `[2020-01-01 00:00:00.123456789, null]`
